the ectopic expression of Escherichia colis serine acetyltranferase (EcSAT) in rice plants results in an increase in the levels of the essential amino acids methionine, cysteines, isoleucin, leucine and valine, and the glutathione pool in the plant.
ectopic expression of an Escherichian coli serine acetytransferase (EcSAT) in transgenic rice plants leads to a significant elevation of cysteins and methionine levels in leaves and seeds.

ectopic expression of an E. coli serine acetytransferase isoform in rice plastids increased the cysteine and free methionine contents of rice seeds, which is important for the nutritional quality of cereals.

the development of a novel strategy for increasing the methionine and cysteine contents of rice grains by overexpressing an enzyme involved in cysteine biosynthesis in plastids.
